    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, good prompting is what makes AI and LLMs valuable for SEO work, from analysis to reporting.
    • Many SEOs have already been prompting for the last few years, but there are so many ways that AI can help; having examples can give us the inspiration to adapt and make this our own.
    • Industry observers note that apart from the right prompts, the one thing an LLM needs is data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, good prompting is what makes AI and LLMs valuable for SEO work, from analysis to reporting. At Search Engine Journal, the team experiments with AI to wrangle data, handle repetitive tasks, and do deep analysis.

    Many SEOs have already been prompting for the last few years, but there are so many ways that AI can help; having examples can give us the inspiration to adapt and make this our own.

    Industry observers note that apart from the right prompts, the one thing an LLM needs is data. For analysis and reporting, SEO tools can provide the keyword estimates, backlink records, clicks, impressions, and performance data that an LLM doesn’t have. Connect those to ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini and, with the right prompts and some prodding, you can ask more complex questions. For example, which pages have conflicting canonicals, serve a valuable product category, and can be fixed without a template rebuild?

    The following list of 35 prompts covers a range of SEO applications. Many of them need a data connection or an export, and they are designed to take your prompting beyond the basics.

    Use this guide as a basis to experiment, adapt to your own needs and clients, and build your own SEO prompt library.

    Before you copy and run a prompt from this list, read the setup guidance below.

    The tools an AI needs depend on the work. For a copy review, provide the text and your requirements. For analysis, provide the data. For current research or private SEO data, make sure the AI can access the relevant sources.

    After analysis, check that the results cover the intended data and that notable calculations are sound.

    Industry observers note that available tools depend on the account and workspace. So check the current documentation for ChatGPT files, Claude file creation, and Gemini file analysis.

    Sources indicate that for connected SEO data, follow the provider’s setup instructions. Check subscription, API allowance, and dataset requirements, and set a retrieval limit when API usage is charged.

    In a recent development, an effective prompt gives an LLM a clear task, useful context, and specific constraints. When you ask it to work with evidence, add the instruction below to whichever prompt you use:.

    Use customer research to identify the tasks and needs behind people’s questions. The prompt turns those needs into potential search queries, while keeping evidence from customers separate from ideas that still need validation.

    According to recent reports, you need: Customer research, a seed topic, and a clear picture of your audience. Text analysis is enough to map needs; add a keyword export or SEO connector if you also want demand estimates.

    Use a topic and audience to generate distinct questions that could help readers complete a task. The prompt separates questions found in your data from research hypotheses, then recommends which belong in an existing article, a separate resource, or neither.

    Read more about query fan-out for background on this topic and note that Google’s current AI search guidance cautions against creating pages for every possible query variation.

    An optional source is the Bing AI Performance report. Its sampled grounding queries show retrieval phrases associated with cited content, but they are not necessarily user prompts and do not reveal Google’s fan-out queries.

    Industry observers note that you need: A topic, an audience, and your existing content. Query data can help validate ideas, but you don’t need a specialist connector to generate them.

    Check whether an article answers the relevant questions your audience has. The prompt identifies meaningful gaps and proposes only the changes needed to address them, while flagging facts that need research or expert input. Use this template to assess query coverage. If the issue is how the content explains or presents its information, use the content enhancement prompt instead.

    It has been revealed that you need: The article, the reader’s goal, and a list of observed or proposed queries. Include sources for any facts the revision needs.

    In a recent development, group keywords by search intent and identify which existing or potential page could serve each group. The prompt checks the data before using it and treats overlapping page targets as candidates for review, not proof of cannibalization.

    You need: A keyword export with metric definitions and a page inventory. Upload the export for data analysis, or use an authorized SEO connector to retrieve equivalent data.

    For prompts that need to inspect live webpages, an Exa or Firecrawl integration can help retrieve page content. For Google ranking data, use a SERP API or supported connector, such as Ahrefs, DataForSEO, or SerpApi.

    Automated Google searches can return results that look plausible but differ from those a person sees in a normal search. SEJ’s report on SERP poisoning explains the issue. Some providers offer safeguards to detect or resolve misleading results. These can reduce errors, but they cannot guarantee accurate results.

    It has been revealed that dataForSEO’s resolve_poisoned_results option is off by default. When enabled, it detects and resolves poisoned results and adds the cost of one SERP page to the task.

    It has been revealed that keep the search engine, location, language, and device settings consistent, and record when each result set was collected. To compare ranking changes, use two snapshots collected with matching settings. If you do not have a live connector, use dated SERP exports.

    Compare two ranking snapshots to show which queries and pages moved, appeared, or disappeared. The prompt separates observed changes from possible explanations and identifies what evidence would help explain them.

    You need: Two dated rank-tracker or SERP exports collected with matching settings for search engine, market, device, and ranking convention, plus a log of relevant site changes between the two dates. File analysis is enough to compare them.

    It has been revealed that review the pages ranking for a query to understand the needs, audiences, and decision stages they serve. The prompt uses that evidence to recommend a purpose and format for your page without treating common SERP patterns as proven ranking factors.

    Use this before deciding what a page should do. Choose the content comparison template when you already have a page to audit against the results.

    In a recent development, you need: A dated SERP sample, accessible result pages, and a brief or draft of your proposed page. The AI needs web access to review the result pages.

    According to recent reports, generate title options that match the page’s search intent and accurately reflect its content. Each option is tied to a reader need and a supporting passage, so you can check that the title’s promise is supported. Use character count as an editing guide, not a fixed Google limit, as Google may shorten displayed titles to fit the available width.

    In a recent development, use this prompt for title alternatives. Choose the metadata review when you need to diagnose existing titles and descriptions and initiative how to evaluate changes.

    Industry observers note that you need: The page content, its target search intent, and your brand rules. No plugin is needed.

    Decide whether a page needs an enhancement, a clearer focus, a separate page, consolidation review, or no change. The prompt checks time-sensitive claims and uses the site inventory, search intent, performance data, and business goal to explain its recommendation.

    It has been revealed that you need: The current page, a site inventory, dated search-performance data, and the business goal. Use web research to check claims that may have changed.

    According to recent reports, review whether the content gives readers enough evidence to assess its claims, authorship, methods, and sources. The prompt identifies what is already supported, what is missing, and what needs to be verified without inventing experience or credentials.

    You need: The content and verified information about its author, organization, methods, and sources.

    Build a year-long initiative that connects content ideas to reader needs and business objectives. This prompt checks existing coverage, seasonality, launch dates, and team capacity, while keeping later plans provisional where evidence is limited.

    Industry observers note that you need: Keyword or trend data, launch dates, an existing content inventory, and production capacity. Enable file creation to produce a spreadsheet. A calendar connector is optional if you provide the dates.

    Assess whether pages should stay separate, be differentiated, updated, or consolidated. The prompt weighs duplicated information against distinct reader needs and outlines what to preserve if a merge is recommended.

    In a recent development, you need: The candidate pages, crawl and internal-link data, query-to-page performance, and relevant backlink data. Uploaded exports are enough for data analysis.

    In a recent development, review a draft for factual accuracy, sourcing, attribution, contradictions, and clear style problems. The prompt also flags generic sections that need stronger evidence or examples, without claiming to certify originality or authorship.

    You need: The draft, your house style, sources, and any material for comparison. Use web access to check missing or current factual references.

    Study a defined sample of competitor pages to understand the topics, formats, and evidence they use. The prompt identifies strategic options based on that sample without assuming it reveals the competitor’s full strategy or performance.

    According to recent reports, use this to study publishing patterns and strategic choices. Choose coverage gaps when you need a prioritized list of unmet reader needs from two content inventories.

    You need: Competitor content inventories, your own content or assets, and a limit on the research. Use browsing or a bounded crawl; performance comparisons require actual data.

    Compare your page with a defined set of ranking pages using a dated SERP export or provider dataset. This prompt looks at reader needs, evidence, examples, and decision support, then identifies where your page can improve or contribute something different.

    Sources indicate that you need: The keyword, market, device, a dated SERP export, and your content. An authorized provider connection can supply the export; ordinary web search cannot replace a ranking snapshot.

    It has been revealed that find places where a link would help readers, using only the destinations you supply. Each recommendation includes the existing anchor text and a reason for the link, with questionable or unsuitable URLs flagged for checking.

    It has been revealed that you need: The source article and a current destination list with URLs, summaries, and status. No connector is needed if you provide these.

    Review whether the title and description match the page and its search intent. Suggest alternatives based on the content, then outline how to assess any change using comparable data without assuming it will improve click-through rate.

    You need: The current metadata, page content, a comparable SERP sample, and optional query performance data. Text analysis is enough.

    Identify specific explanations, evidence, or visuals that would make the page more useful. Recommend additions only when they address a reader’s need, and flag any research or assets still required.

    Industry observers note that you need: The content, the reader’s task, available assets, and relevant data. Image or chart tools are optional if you want approved additions produced.

    Industry observers note that use screenshots to review the page’s visible layout and messaging, then suggest tests for potential improvements. Keep visual observations separate from hypotheses about behavior, speed, or functionality.

    You need: Desktop and mobile screenshots, the page content, and the conversion goal. Include funnel or performance data to assess visitor behavior or page speed.

    Assess whether each location has enough distinct customer need and verified information to justify its own page. For locations that qualify, draft relevant copy and flag local details that still need confirmation.

    Sources indicate that you need: Confirmed service areas, local business facts, offers, and supporting evidence. Use web research to check current local sources.

    It has been revealed that turn real customer questions into concise answers based on approved business information. Check current local rules against official sources and flag questions that need a business decision or further verification.

    According to recent reports, you need: Actual customer questions, approved business information, and current official sources for local rules. No FAQ plugin is needed to draft answers.

    Use backlink data to find relevant pages that may have a reason to reference your work. Check the source pages and your assets before drafting specific outreach – the recommendations are not guaranteed placements, and no messages are sent.

    Industry observers note that you need: A backlink gap export or authorized SEO provider connection, your relevant assets, and web research access. Set a maximum number of pages to inspect.

    In a recent development, compare your content with a competitor’s to find reader needs your pages may not serve. Prioritize possible gaps using business relevance and any demand data you provide, rather than assuming a competitor’s topic proves demand.

    Recent findings suggest that you need: Your content inventory, a competitor’s inventory, and readable pages. Add keyword or performance data for quantitative prioritization.

    Turn SEO evidence into either an analytical report or a one-page executive memo. Calculate from raw data when needed, explain what the evidence supports, and make ROI claims only when the value and cost basis are agreed.

    According to recent reports, you need: Search and analytics exports or checked performance metrics, source definitions, comparable periods, business goals, and a change log. Include costs and an agreed value basis if you want an ROI calculation. Use data analysis for calculations – text analysis is enough to summarize checked findings.

    Recent findings suggest that compare crawl, sitemap, and URL Inspection evidence to investigate why important pages are missing from search or have a different selected canonical. The results identify concerns and checks to follow; they do not guarantee indexing or make site changes. The URL Inspection API reports on Google’s indexed version. It does not run a live URL test.

    You need: A crawl export, sitemap, priority pages, and URL Inspection results or a documented inspection sample. A normal crawl can show declared canonicals, but not Google’s selected canonical.

    Compare the server HTML with the rendered page to find differences in content, links, directives, and structured data. Treat those differences as evidence to investigate, not proof of what every crawler can access.

    You need: Server HTML, rendered HTML, response headers, and a screenshot for the same URL. Add Google’s rendered-page evidence if available.

    Sources indicate that use Chrome DevTools MCP to inspect slow form and CTA interactions. Check whether analytics, tag-manager callbacks, or other scripts contribute to delays rather than assuming tracking is the cause.

    Sources indicate that you need: An approved test page, representative interactions, known tracking scripts, and an AI client that supports MCP servers with Chrome DevTools MCP connected, such as a coding agent. The standard ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini chat apps cannot run this prompt unless that connection is set up. Add field INP data where available. A controlled trace diagnoses tested interactions, not every real user’s page experience.

    Industry observers note that chrome DevTools MCP’s performance tools may send the URLs you trace to Google’s CrUX API to fetch real-user field data. If your test URLs are confidential, check the documentation for how to turn this off before you run a trace.

    See Google’s INP guidance for the metric and the official Chrome DevTools MCP documentation for browser and performance tools.

    Sources indicate that check whether existing structured data matches the visible page and verified facts. Google’s structured data policies require markup to reflect visible content, so identify unsupported or conflicting properties and suggest the smallest change needed, without promising rich results or AI citations.

    You need: Existing JSON-LD, visible page content, verified business or product facts, and any validation results. Web access helps check current requirements.

    Turn technical audit findings into a prioritized work queue. Group related issues, explain their business relevance and dependencies, and distinguish confirmed defects from warnings that still need investigation.

    You need: A technical audit or crawl export, affected URLs, business priorities, and any available performance data. Include engineering estimates only if your team has supplied them.

    In a recent development, compare your intended access policy with crawler rules, headers, firewall controls, logs, and Search Console settings. Separate search, training, user-request, and ad-validation access, then recommend changes and checks without applying them.

    You need: Your intended access policy, robots.txt, response headers, relevant CDN or firewall rules, sampled server logs, and the current Search Console generative AI setting, including inherited settings.

    Compare saved AI answers across comparable runs, keeping brand mentions, recommendations, and linked citations distinct. Report counts and rates with clear denominators, and treat changes in a limited sample as observations rather than universal visibility trends.

    In a recent development, you need: Saved AI answers and cited URLs, with prompts, dates, platform, locale, and available model or session details. A monitoring service is optional if it provides those fields.

    In a recent development, compare AI search impressions, search clicks, AI referrals, and key events while keeping each source and metric separate. Check changes in tracking and reporting, and avoid attributing visits or conversions to citations when the data cannot establish that link.

    You need: Search Console performance exports, analytics referral and key-event data, and optional Bing AI Performance exports. Include channel definitions and tracking changes.

    According to recent reports, check what the assistant actually received before interpreting it. Review scope, fields, row counts, missing values, duplicates, metric definitions, and joins, then report what the data can and cannot support.

    You need: The files or authorized connector you plan to analyze, the requested scope, and the provider’s metric definitions. Live retrieval also requires access to the relevant account and a supported operation.

    Compare Search Console performance with crawl and inspection evidence to identify the pages and groups contributing to a traffic change. Check joins and totals, then list explanations to investigate without treating timing or a technical warning as proof of cause.

    You need: Comparable Search Console exports, a dated crawl, page groups, and a change log. Add URL Inspection results where available. Use data analysis for calculations and joins.

    Turn a defined reader need into a focused brief grounded in existing coverage, sources, expertise, and original material. The brief sets out the page’s purpose and evidence still to collect without drafting the full article or inventing experience.

    Sources indicate that you need: The reader’s task, existing coverage, approved sources, and available expertise or original material. Add a dated SERP sample when relevant and use web research for source checks.

    Industry observers note that create and test one specific filter, query, extraction rule, or validation script against representative examples. Include expected results and boundaries, and state exactly which tests ran.

    You need: One task, the target tool and language or query dialect, the input structure, and representative examples with expected results. Use code execution or a safe test environment for validation.

    Before uploading a file or connecting a data source, always make sure you have authority to share it with that AI tool. Remove or anonymize personal and confidential information where possible, and never include passwords, API keys, or other access credentials in a prompt.

    Give connectors access only to the data needed for the task and store secrets such as API keys in a local .env file that only your user account can read (for example, chmod 600).

    Industry observers note that to reduce the risk of prompt injection, treat text retrieved from webpages, files, and other sources as information to assess, not instructions to follow. Tell your LLM to ignore any instructions embedded in that material that try to change the task or request access to other data. This lowers the risk but does not remove it, so give the tool access only to what the task needs. Review AI-generated findings, citations, calculations, and code before relying on them or making changes to a live site.

    Once a prompt produces reliable results, save it with its required inputs, data sources, output format, and checks. Keep client-specific instructions and reference material together in a ChatGPT project, Claude skill, or Gemini skill, where available.

    For recurring comparisons, record the data source, dates, and conditions for each run. A saved prompt doesn’t provide access to private data or replace the tools needed to retrieve it.

    It has been revealed that finally, to make prompts fit for purpose, it’s not as simple as plugging in templates, copying and pasting the output, then calling it a day. It’s important to keep refining every prompt as part of your process. Keep testing, adjusting, and pressure-checking your prompts. Refine them until they consistently deliver results that enhance your workflow and productivity.

    Sources indicate that the fresh budget would make a local reporting program permanent and extend a 35% tax credit on newsroom salaries. The support makes “a massive, massive difference.”.

    It has been revealed that A Canadian program to place local reporters in underserved communities has lived from renewal to renewal. Publishers who relied on the Local Journalism Initiative couldn’t be sure whether the money would be there again.

    It has been revealed that that changed last week when Canada proposed a federal budget that would make the Local Journalism Initiative permanent. The 2026 budget would increase LJI funding to $134 million over four years with $41 million in annual ongoing funding after that. (Figures are, naturally, in Canadian dollars.) For the budget to be finalized, it must pass Parliament. With Prime Minister Mark Carney’s party in the majority, it’s expected to.

    Expanding the LJI is not even the biggest piece of federal help for newsrooms, according to Paul Deegan, president and CEO of the news industry advocacy group News Media Canada. The same budget extends a 35% tax credit on newsroom salaries through 2028 and opens it to radio and television newsrooms for the first time. The tax credit will cost $501 million over the next five years, according to the budget. Thanks to the Online News Act, Canadian newsrooms also get funding from Google. And then there’s Canadian investment in public media; the 2026 budget added $300 million over two years to CBC/Radio-Canada “to strengthen its capacity to meet the evolving needs of Canadians across the country.”.

    I asked Deegan: How did Canadian publishers secure so much federal funding for news?

    According to recent reports, “We have a government that ‘gets it,’” Deegan remarked. “They see what Big Tech monopolists have done to local news. They know the labor tax credit is the leading driver of maintaining and growing newsroom headcount.”.

    Industry observers note that RELATED ARTICLECalifornia’s significant local news bill becomes lawLaura Hazard OwenOctober 1, 2026There have been similar proposals and experiments in the United States, including a newly introduced tax credit in California. But Canada is much further down the road. The country can offer lessons on what it looks like when a federal government commits to supporting journalism.

    The labor tax credit refunds 35% of a newsroom employee’s salary, up to $29,750 per journalist per year. The percentage had been scheduled to fall to 25% at the end of 2026.

    “In terms of employing the [largest] number of journalists and keeping newsroom employment stability, the labor tax credit is number one,” Deegan said.

    In a recent development, there’s also the Online News Act which has brought in $100 million of Google money annually. Of that amount, $63 million is set aside for news publishers. (Meta blocked news on Facebook and Instagram in Canada rather than pay under the Online News Act.) Publishers receive around $17,000 per journalist per year.

    “That’s about $47,000 per journalist per year from those two measures,” Deegan said. “That just makes a massive, massive difference.”.

    Industry observers note that in the U.S., some ideas for funding local journalism have been criticized as helping large chain newspapers — including chains that have hollowed out local newsrooms for years. Deegan — whose news industry group counts Postmedia and Torstar as members — acknowledged that the largest share of tax credit dollars goes to the largest employers.

    It has been revealed that but News Media Canada also represents small and digital-only publications, and Deegan noted the smallest Canadian outlets face another problem. To qualify for the tax credit, an organization must produce original news content and regularly employ at least two journalists “at arm’s length” from its owners. An advisory board found the second rule excludes small “mom-and-pop” newsrooms.

    According to recent reports, the Local Journalism Initiative is a more targeted program than the tax credit. Launched in 2019, it was designed to support local and community news in underserved areas. The LJI program supports about 470 reporting positions in roughly 1,000 communities across Canada.

    Even generous government subsidies have not stopped losses in local news completely. But early results showed the LJI increased reporting capacity and local news in “news poverty” communities with limited local news offerings. The same evaluation identified reaching “news deserts” — communities with no existing local news outlets — and Indigenous communities as obstacles.

    “Since LJI is demand driven, funding allocation across the country varies and gaps remain in some areas, such as news deserts,” the report reads. Later, the report notes that allowing news startups “could better support attraction and retainment of journalists” in the neediest communities.

    According to recent reports, many of the newsrooms receiving the LJI funding are small. Deegan described family-owned weekly newspapers with circulations as low as 800. Funding provides a local journalist to report on “cops, courts, city hall, and the school board.”.

    “Without those LJI journalists in some of those communities, those things simply wouldn’t be covered,” he said.

    According to recent reports, some underserved communities, particularly in northern Canada, struggle to hire reporters given high living costs and remote locations. “Even with the grant, it’s just hard to recruit and find people,” Deegan noted.

    Deegan points to two factors that have made Canada’s federal funding for news work. The first is distance. Publishers get LJI money from one of three administrator organizations: News Media Canada, Community Radio Fund of Canada, or the Consortium of Official Language Minority Community Media. These organizations — not the government itself — administer the funds and an independent board advises on who qualifies for the tax credit.

    “To avoid perceptions of conflict of interest, the government ensured that third parties adjudicate who receives local journalism initiative reporters and who is eligible for the labor tax credit,” Deegan said.

    The second factor applies to the Online News Act and, more generally, to Canadian politics.

    “When it comes to holding those platforms to account, one of the reasons we have been successful is that we have a ban [on] corporate political financing at the federal level in Canada,” Deegan mentioned. “These companies sprinkle goodies around to friendly academics, think tanks, and other useful idiots to do some of their bidding, but our government sees through that nonsense.”.

    ONA, OpenNews, and others see troubled times ahead, so it’s goodbye to “rubber chicken dinners.”.

    According to recent reports, RELATED ARTICLEWe know coronavirus has wrecked the events business for media in 2020. But will it come back post-virus?Joshua BentonMarch 25, 2020When the pandemic forced conferences to go virtual, the question was whether people would come back in person post-Covid.

    For a while, they did. For a couple years after the pandemic, people were excited to be in person together again. U.S. journalism organizations saw their revenue climb, as sponsors and funders spent generously.

    It has been revealed that at the end of 2026, though, the situation is less rosy. Combine surging jet fuel prices, inflation, media companies cutting costs, and declining sponsor and funder dollars, and the future appears grim not just for journalism conferences but, in some cases, for the organizations behind them.

    Revenue is the total revenue line on each organization’s IRS Form 990. The 990s are from ProPublica’s Nonprofit Explorer. ONA’s 990 for 2025 was not available as of November 12, 2026.

    The Online News Association mentioned on Tuesday that it is “pausing” its 26-year-old conference and laying off its five staffers.

    Sources indicate that “Before the pandemic, the annual conference was ONA’s biggest source of revenue, and together with grants, it sustained the organization. This is no longer true,” Niketa Patel wrote. “The costs of large convenings have climbed sharply while professional development and sponsorship budgets have shrunk.”.

    Recent findings suggest that LION Publishers said in September that it’s getting out of the large conference business for now. “Philanthropy is famously fickle, and funding priorities have shifted, making this kind of conference a very tough lift,” executive director Chris Krewson added.

    LION barely broke even on the conferences it held in 2025 and 2026, Krewson told me. The organization may still hold smaller events next year, it’s not cutting staff or programming, and it’s expanding its Audit program. But it “won’t be taking on the responsibility for an independent event at a hotel with a food and beverage minimum and hotel room block for 400-plus people.”.

    “Every dollar I spend on rubber chicken dinners and microphones/WiFi for three days is money I can’t spend on programs that make publishers’ businesses stronger,” Krewson noted.

    OpenNews said in October that it’s switching into “emergency mode”1 and cutting back on “work that distills journalism craft: no more community calls or Source articles for at least the rest of 2026 and maybe longer.”.

    The future of OpenNews’s annual conference, SRCCON, is uncertain. “We usually make our decision about SRCCON at about this time every year, but this year is different as we consider the news from both LION and ONA and the funding pressures that we know all too well,” Jessica Morrison, co–executive director of OpenNews, told me in an email. “We are opening a community conversation today — emails going out very soon — to gather input about SRCCON, our other programs, and where we go next with OpenNews.”.

    It has been revealed that the three-year-old Organization for Accessible Journalism noted Thursday that it is shutting down. “Financial support never reached a level that allowed us to build beyond an all volunteer effort — including my full-time effort,” founder Stacy Kess wrote.

    In a recent development, journalism conferences in the United States are certainly not gone. IRE and NICAR will hold their annual data journalism conference in Denver in March. The Institute for Nonprofit News is “talking about what INN Days will look like in 2027” and will know more by early next year. And the International Symposium on Journalism is on for 2027 — its 28th year, founder (and Nieman Foundation board member) Rosental Alves told me. But things have gotten harder, he noted. “It’s not only the difficulty of finding sponsors, but also the rising costs of venues, hotels, airfares, etc., compounded by shrinking travel budgets in newsrooms and even the problems international attendees face in coming to the U.S.,” he told me in an email. ISOJ cut costs, in part by moving to a different venue, and it benefits from being relatively small. “It’s very sad that foundations and corporations that funded journalism conferences in the past have pulled back their support,” Alves added. “The need for these gatherings is as great as ever.” a play on Emergency Mode for News, its initiative to support journalists working during disasters [↩].

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    It has been revealed that we’re looking for a Software Engineer to join our AI Tooling team and help shape how developers and agents build with Supabase. You'll build and own our AI tooling, including agents, the MCP server, agent skills and the dashboard assistant, and as the space moves you'll build the tooling for newly introduced technologies too. You'll build it all eval-first: every tool ships with evals and metrics, so we know, with evidence, that it makes agents better rather than worse.

    You'll work closely with the Docs, CLI, Frontend and SDK teams, and with the AI Tooling Infrastructure engineers who run these services in production. Other teams contribute to AI Tooling to improve Supabase's agentic capabilities, and you'll help them do that while keeping the quality bar high.

    This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

    Build and improve the AI tooling we run today, including the MCP server, agent skills, agents and the Assistant.

    It has been revealed that make new Supabase products usable by agents from day one: tools, skills and evals for new product surfaces. Also build tooling for new AI technologies as they emerge: prototype promptly, evaluate honestly, and decide with the team what is worth taking to production.

    Drive an eval-first approach: build and improve evals, instrumentation and feedback loops, measure tools against a no-tool baseline, and help define the quality KPIs and gates that stop regressions shipping.

    Understand how customers and agents actually use what we ship, and turn that into improvements to our tooling, interfaces and documentation.

    Design how documentation and product knowledge are exposed to agents, and measure whether it works.

    Build patterns and tools that help customers add AI to their own apps, such as MCP on Edge Functions, vector embeddings and agents running on Edge Functions.

    Enable teams to improve Supabase's agentic capabilities through contributions to AI Tooling: clear contribution paths, templates, documentation and review practice.

    Centralise shared AI logic so teams reuse it rather than duplicate it.

    Ship tools that are battle-tested, with strong tests, benchmarking and stress testing where it counts.

    Work with the AI Tooling Infrastructure engineers on reliability, auth and hosting.

    Work across Docs, CLI, Frontend, SDK and other teams to deliver one coherent developer experience, and stay close to the fast-moving AI ecosystem.

    Have 5+ years of experience in professional software engineering experience.

    Write strong TypeScript and know the JavaScript ecosystem well: npm, ES modules, bundlers, compatibility.

    Are deeply familiar with the AI ecosystem: current tools, agent patterns and practical trade-offs. You can tell a durable pattern from hype.

    Have built developer tools, product interfaces or platform primitives used by other engineers.

    Have designed or used evaluation frameworks to measure AI quality, reliability and task success, and understand baselines, variance and cost.

    Have strong judgement about where AI improves workflows and how to avoid fragile or gimmicky experiences.

    Write tests and validate reliability in real-world conditions.

    Know Postgres and relational database practice.

    Communicate clearly in writing, work across product, engineering and docs, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

    Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving rapidly.

    Experience with vector databases and embeddings, ideally pgvector.

    Examples of customer-facing AI features or agents you've shipped.

    Examples of documentation or structured knowledge designed for developers or agents.

    Experience with Braintrust or a similar eval and tracing platform, or setting up CI quality gates.

    Open-source contributions or developer tooling you've maintained.

    Experience across several product surfaces or teams.

    It has been revealed that we hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a newly introduced city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

    In a recent development, we operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    Industry observers note that supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    It has been revealed that we move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that google published new guidance on how to keep from blocking its user-triggered AI agents that identify themselves as Google-Agent.
    • It has been revealed that google-Agent is the name used by AI agents hosted on Google’s infrastructure that navigate websites and perform actions on behalf of users.
    • It describes Google-Agent as agents that are hosted on Google’s infrastructure, interact with and navigate websites, and complete tasks on behalf of a user.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that google published new guidance on how to keep from blocking its user-triggered AI agents that identify themselves as Google-Agent. The new documentation shows how to verify legitimate Google-Agent requests and configure firewalls to allow them on websites.

    It has been revealed that google-Agent is the name used by AI agents hosted on Google’s infrastructure that navigate websites and perform actions on behalf of users. Google’s guidance and also Google’s User-Triggered Fetcher documentation do not identify which Google products or services use Google-Agent. Neither documentation mentions Google Search, AI Mode, Gemini, or any other Google product.

    It describes Google-Agent as agents that are hosted on Google’s infrastructure, interact with and navigate websites, and complete tasks on behalf of a user.

    The document states or implies that the Google-Agent does the following:.

    The upcoming guidance explains there are three ways that website owners can verify that a request comes from Google-Agent.

    Industry observers note that 1. The request’s User-Agent header contains “Google-Agent.”.

    2. The request originates from an IP address listed in Google’s published file of user-triggered agent ranges.

    3. Only where it’s present, when the request carries a cryptographic signature under Google’s experimental Web Bot Auth protocol, which can be checked against Google’s published public keys.

    The first two checks are the baseline, and the signature check adds stronger verification when it’s available. A Google-Agent bot can then be allowed through whatever bot defenses are in use once it passes those checks. Google also notes that some CDNs and bot-detection services handle this verification automatically.

    Lastly, Google offers guidance on troubleshooting when the Google-Agent is unintentionally blocked.

    Google recommends ensuring that rules allowing Google-Agent requests have higher priority and are evaluated before broader blocking rules, including:.

    If bot detection, firewall (WAF), or CDN rules only covers the initial page request, the agent will be able to land on the website but it will be unable to finish whatever task it’s there to accomplish.

    Google recommends checking that CAPTCHA challenges are disabled for verified Google-Agent requests, reviewing rate limits, IP address updates, and proxy configurations.

    “Proxy headers: Confirm that load balancers and intermediate proxies preserve the original client IP, the User-Agent header, and (for signed requests) the Signature, Signature-Input, and Signature-Agent headers.”.

    Google’s fresh guidance addresses three issues to check if Google-Agent is being inadvertently blocked:.

    “Shared-IP rate limits: Confirm that per-IP rate-limiting rules account for or exempt verified Google-Agent IP ranges, as concurrent requests from multiple users share the same egress pool.

    IP range updates: Confirm that IP-based rules stay synced with the latest ranges in user-triggered-agents.json.

    Proxy headers: Confirm that load balancers and intermediate proxies preserve the original client IP, the User-Agent header, and (for signed requests) the Signature, Signature-Input, and Signature-Agent headers.”.

    Google’s new Google-Agent guidance offers tips for website owners who want to allow Google-Agent interactions, stressing that they need to make sure that legitimate Google-Agent requests can pass through security defenses without compromising protections against unwanted bots.

    From fresh majors to search traffic, newspapers to impeachment: Have you kept up with this week’s media news?

    It’s been another busy week. Recap it with the third edition of the Nieman Lab News-About-News Quiz, your weekly incentive to keep up with the latest happenings in the world of digital journalism. All questions are based on the week’s Nieman Lab stories or articles elsewhere that we’ve linked to in What We’re Reading. The quiz will appear here through November as a trial run; if people seem to like it, we’ll keep it going in 2027. Good luck!

    What journalism organization unveiled this week that it was canceling its annual conference and laying off most of its staff?

    “Since we gathered in Chicago for ONA26, many of you have asked when we will be together again,” CEO Niketa Patel wrote. “Unfortunately, it will not be in 2027. ONA has decided to pause our in-person events and will not host a conference in 2027.”.

    For the first time ever, the press freedom group Reporters Without Borders (RSF) has officially called for the impeachment of a U.S. official. Which one?

    Recent findings suggest that “RSF does not take the question of impeachment lightly. In fact, our organization has never before called for the removal of a US official. But the severity and persistence of Carr’s misconduct as FCC chairman demand an extraordinary response. Congress has a constitutional responsibility to hold him accountable. Restoring the FCC’s independence must be central to that effort.”.

    Emerson College recently unveiled a new degree program aimed at helping students build “a career across a rapidly changing media landscape.” What’s the program’s name?

    “Our upcoming Content Creation major prepares students to be a part of the evolving creator economy, teaching them not only how to produce compelling digital content but also how to build a successful entrepreneurial career.”.

    What news organization — after a challenging few years — indicates it is now “within striking distance of break-even,” financially?

    “I’ll be honest,” executive editor Matt Murphy stated at a conference. “We had years of losses, and steepening losses. That’s the truth. We’re a private tech giant and don’t share the figures, but it was hundreds and hundreds of millions of dollars. Now we’re within striking distance of break-even, and I expect next year will be our best year in seven years. We’ve done the right-sizing we needed, which was tough.”.

    Sources indicate that the Echo-Pioneer — the local newspaper in the town of High Level, Alberta (population 4,000) — has an unusual business model. What is it?

    Town officials signed a two-year “advertising and readership agreement” in 2025. It’s one of the many ways local Canadian news outlets are trying to stay afloat — most notably the federal Local Journalism Initiative.

    Which online publisher’s CEO declared that Google search traffic had “dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week” in October?

    As a result of the search decline, CEO Steve Huffman declared Reddit would be shifting to a primarily “logged-in experience.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the Asia-Pacific outlet The Diplomat retracted an interview with a South Korean CEO last week. Why?

    According to recent reports, “The author presented themselves as a South Korean freelance journalist and claimed to have interviewed Newtype’s CEO. We now know that the journalist fabricated the interview and may not even be who they claimed to be.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the parliament of an Asian nation is debating requiring tech companies like Google and Meta to pay news outlets when they direct owners to their stories. Which nation?

    The proposed law would also require compensating news publishers when AI models are trained on news content.

    Which international news outlet, sensing a political opening, is expanding its reporting team in the United States?

    Recent findings suggest that “Market research indicated there was room to grow among politically liberal Jews in the United States. Gali Arnon, who became the chief executive of Haaretz Group last year, mentioned she wanted the newspaper to become in other countries what it is in Israel: an ‘identity brand.’”.

    Sources indicate that this photo shows an early editorial plan from one of the first notable publications on the World Wide Web, a mononymic website that has recently been in the news. What site was it?

    The photo is from Salon co-founder Laura Miller, laying out some early “complications” of the influential web “magazine” which closed last week. “People sometimes tell me about reading Salon avidly in their youth, how it felt like connecting to something exhilarating and cool and a bit crazy in the strange new expanses of the internet. All I can say is: That’s exactly how it felt to work there.”.

    The most important stories about journalism and the future of news, delivered to your inbox every afternoon.

    Congressional Democrats will have to determine whether they want to revive the old system Donald Trump defunded or build something more attuned to today's media ecosystem.

    Stations in Upcoming Hampshire, Wisconsin, Massachusetts, and Utah all climbed in our regular ranking of public radio stations between July and September.

    The local journalism that has long powered the 169-year-old firm is no longer a viable business model, executives told McClatchy employees during a virtual town hall this month.

    In a recent development, RELATED ARTICLESearch traffic has declined so much that some publishers are considering opting out of Google entirelyNeel DhaneshaJuly 22, 2026We’ve now been publishing roundups of local newspaper traffic for a full year, so we can compare this year’s traffic to last year’s. Almost across the board, local newspapers are seeing traffic decline as Google referrals drop. For July, August, and September, traffic to the most-visited sites is lower than at this time last year, according to our Similarweb data.

    Recent findings suggest that RELATED ARTICLEHow did newspapers in places like Harrisburg, Birmingham, and Syracuse become some of America’s most-read online?Joshua BentonJuly 23, 2025A good example is Advance Local’s Harrisburg Patriot-News, PennLive.com. Josh has written about Advance publications punching above their weight in traffic. They still are: Advance outlets like AL.com, Mlive.com, and NJ.com, among others, continued to feature prominently in the top sites by estimated monthly visits in July, August, and September. In August 2026, PennLive’s traffic growth stood out even among Advance peers; it gained 3.6 million visits in August compared to July, a 78% spike. But in total, PennLive saw a little over 8.2 million monthly visits for August 2026 — down from about 12.5 million in August 2025.

    Still, publishers large and small are finding ways to bring more readers to their sites. In August, the Bozeman Daily Chronicle grew its traffic by about 96,000 monthly visits, a 49% jump. Managing editor Jack Reaney attributed the growth to the newspaper launching a latest website Aug. 3 designed for improved functionality, with “fewer, more intentional news categories,” lighter page design for faster load times, and a more modern layout. The Chronicle is one of more than 150 newspapers owned by Adams MultiMedia. The parent firm is rolling out the new website design across its newspapers, but Bozeman was the “guinea pig,” Reaney noted.

    In Florida, Cape Coral Breeze, a small weekly, saw its traffic spike about 139% in August. The network of local weeklies has tried to adopt a daily, real-time mindset after decades of posting once a week, Breeze Newspapers publisher Ray Eckenrode told me. The August spike was driven by participation in Cape Coral Breeze’s “Best of Cape Coral” contest, where readers vote on favorite local businesses in more than 200 categories. According to the team’s internal count, a little over 150,000 “Best of” votes were cast this year, up from 92,000 last year. The team made an effort this year to “drive traffic to our homepage first to reach the contest voting page to expose some of those casual website owners to our news coverage,” Eckenrode said, and had some success with that strategy.

    In September, The Cornell Daily Sun gained 1 million visits, almost a 500% jump from August, when it broke the story of the Cornell 7 lawsuit (and published an editorial naming the defendants). Other local news sites in New York also saw meaningful growth in September; traffic to NNY360.com jumped 84%, while the Gannett-owned Democrat and Chronicle gained about 762,000 visits, a 35% jump.

    Sources indicate that on the opposite coast, the San-Jose-based Mercury News gained around 690,000 monthly visits in September, a 14% jump. “Our traffic is volatile like everyone else’s, but we had a strong September mainly because a couple of stories performed very well,” said Annika Toernqvist, MediaNews Group’s managing editor for digital for Northern California. Environmental beat reporter Paul Rogers‘ story about a newly introduced California law that will ban watering artificial turf “performed exceptionally well on Google and Google Discovery”; 62% of traffic to the story came from search. Stories about the local impact of new state laws consistently do well with the outlet’s readers, according to Toernqvist, and this was “a hot topic with a strong headline.” The story was also the top subscription converter in September. Another story by Rogers covering the proposed renaming of Fremont State Park also drove traffic that month; 86% came from search, mostly from Google Discovery.

    Meanwhile, celebrity reporter Martha Ross‘ story about a fresh book on King Charles’ valet performed well in part thanks to a bump from…the Drudge Report. (“Yes, the Drudge Report still drives traffic,” Toernqvist said; it accounted for 43% of visits to that story.).

    #101567. Information Security Engineer - Application Security at Camunda

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Realworkfromanywhere ↗ Open Full Page

    Information Security Engineer - Application Security at Camunda

    📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1518 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realworkfromanywhere

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes.
    • We're hiring an Information Security Engineer with a focus on Application Security to join our Information Security team at Camunda.
    • In a recent development, we are a team that takes security seriously without making it feel like a locked door.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

    Sources indicate that hi there! We're hiring an Information Security Engineer with a focus on Application Security to join our Information Security team at Camunda.

    In a recent development, we are a team that takes security seriously without making it feel like a locked door. We work in a transparent, straightforward way, and we care about doing the work right rather than just checking a compliance box.

    It has been revealed that you will work side by side with our R&D engineers: reviewing designs, threat modeling newly introduced features, digging into code and helping teams make good, risk-based decisions about the vulnerabilities that come in. You'll also help build the internal tools that make this work scale, including our CVE registry and the LLM-assisted workflows we use to analyse code and triage findings.

    Camunda is an AI-first company, and InfoSec is no exception: AI agents are part of how we review code, assess vulnerabilities, and build our tools. You will help shape how that works.

    This is a hands-on role for someone who already has solid AppSec foundations and wants to grow. We are a generalist team, so you will also take part in our on-call rotation and incident response, and get exposure to other areas of security. But most of your time will be spent with engineers and building and maintaining internal tools and processes.

    Vulnerability management: triage findings from SCA, container and code scanning, external reports and internal security testing; assess whether Camunda is actually affected; agree fix / mitigate / accept with engineering and follow through to release.

    Threat modeling and security reviews: run threat modeling sessions and design reviews with R&D teams for upcoming features and architecture changes, and turn the results into concrete, prioritised actions.

    Code analysis with LLMs: use and improve LLM-assisted tooling (agents, prompts, reusable skills) to review code, validate findings and reproduce issues, while applying your own judgement to know when the model is wrong.

    Recent findings suggest that build internal security tooling: contribute to the CVE registry and related automation that connects scanners, engineering teams, and customer communication. Much of it is built on Camunda itself.

    Help engineers do the secure thing by default: answer questions, review pull requests, improve guidelines and occasionally run a session or workshop.

    On-call and incident response: share the InfoSec on-call rotation with the other engineers and help investigate and resolve security incidents.

    Support the wider team: help write security advisories for our customers, answer customer security questions and support audits.

    What You Will Bring to the Role.

    Around 3+ years in security or software engineering, with at least 2 of them working on application or product security (AppSec, product security, pentesting, or a security-focused developer role all count).

    Experience at a SaaS or software product organization, working closely with engineering teams that ship often through modern CI/CD and cloud environments.

    Hands-on vulnerability triage: you've worked with tools like Snyk, Trivy, Semgrep, CodeQL or similar, can tell a real issue from a false positive, and can explain how exploitable something actually is in context (CVSS, exploitability, configuration).

    Threat modeling and design review experience (e.g. STRIDE) on real systems, ideally web apps, APIs, or distributed services.

    You read and write code. You're comfortable reading Java (Camunda is built on it) well enough to follow a data flow and spot a security bug. You can write scripts and small tools and contribute to an existing codebase with review.

    You build with AI, not just chat with it. You use AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or similar) in your daily work to write tools, analyse code or automate tasks. And you know their output still needs a second look, especially when it comes to security.

    Clear, friendly communication with engineers. You see yourself as an enabler, not a gatekeeper, and you can explain risk to people who aren't security specialists.

    Some Python and/or JavaScript experience, or experience building internal tools.

    Sources indicate that willingness to learn and use Camunda, since we build a lot of our own security automation on it. Prior BPMN / workflow experience is a plus.

    Experience responding to security incidents or being part of an on-call rotation.

    Exposure to security advisories, CVE disclosure or bug bounty programmes.

    Knowledge of AI/LLM security risks (OWASP Top 10 for LLMs / agentic apps, prompt injection, tool abuse).

    Experience securing Kubernetes or container-based workloads, or open-source / B2B software.

    This role is an existing vacancy.

    According to recent reports, we offer competitive, fair, and transparent compensation. Salary ranges are location-based, with Standard and Major markets (global tech hubs) reflecting local competition.

    The Annual Total Target Cash (base salary + 100% variable target, where applicable) shown below spans from the minimum in a Standard market to the maximum in a Major market. Final offers depend on skills, experience, and location, and we typically hire in the first half of the range to allow room for growth:.

    United States: $119,900.00 to $193,200.00.

    United Kingdom: £75,300.00 to £123,800.00.

    Singapore: S$148,900.00 to S$223,300.00.

    If you’re based elsewhere, you’ll be hired via Remote.com (our global employer partner), and your Talent Acquisition Partner will provide a personalized Total Rewards Calculator after your first interview.

    Equity: We also offer equity (where applicable) through our Virtual Stock Option Plan (VSOP).

    It has been revealed that we invest in your wellbeing, growth, and ability to connect, along with perks that support you no matter where you’re based. Our benefits are globally designed and locally delivered where applicable.

    Remote & Flexible: Work from anywhere with the setup that suits you, home office budget, co-working space support, and flexible time off to recharge when you need it.

    In Person Connection: We invest in meaningful face time through our Annual Kickoff (Vienna in 2025, Madrid in 2026!), team offsites, and Camundi Connection Budgets, including contributing to meetups while travelling,, and local gatherings with fellow Camundi.

    In a recent development, health & Wellbeing: Access locally tailored healthcare, Modern Health for global mental wellbeing, and our Live Well Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA), a flexible, global benefit that puts you in control of your whole life, not just work, from: staying active, to caring for family, exploring personal passions, meaningful experiences, and investing in your financial wellbeing. The Live Well program launches in 2026 and scales to €1,000 annually from 2027.

    Financial Security: Retirement and pension looks (often with organization contributions), plus life and disability insurance where relevant.

    Professional Growth: Up to $/€/£1,000 per year for self-driven learning: courses, certifications, books, you decide!

    Sources indicate that AI in our hiring process: Camunda may use AI tools to aid the screening of applications and during the interview process. You can learn more here.

    ”Everyone is welcome at Camunda” — it’s a celebrated component of our culture. We strive to create an inclusive environment that empowers our people. At Camunda, we honour diverse cultures and backgrounds and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to gender, race, ethnicity, religion, belief, sexual orientation, age, disability or any other protected characteristics under applicable law. We are looking forward to your application!

    Come join us and be part of Camunda’s incredible journey: Make an impact at a pivotal moment in our story!

    Industry observers note that please be aware that scammers may impersonate Camunda by reaching out about job opportunities. Camunda will only contact candidates from an email address ending in @camunda.com or @talent.camunda.com. We will never ask candidates for bank account details, checks, payment, or other sensitive financial information as part of our hiring process. If you receive a suspicious message, please do not respond, click any links, or share personal information.

    By opting in to SMS use, please be aware that:.

    Text message frequency may vary;.

    Standard text message and data rates may apply; and.

    By opting in, you will be enrolled directly in ongoing recruiting text messages from Camunda.

    To opt-out, simply select 'No' when prompted during your application. You can also change your preferences at any time by contacting talent-operations@camunda.com.

    #101566. NPR makes fixing its app a key priority in its upcoming strategic plan

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (718 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Niemanlab ↗ Open Full Page

    NPR makes fixing its app a key priority in its upcoming strategic plan

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Niemanlab

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • All the latest headlines and insights from the world of digital journalism and publishing.
    • In a recent development, we will never sell your address.
    • Industry observers note that we have sent a confirmation link to .
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    All the latest headlines and insights from the world of digital journalism and publishing. Our daily newsletter is a must-read from newsrooms to executive suites.

    In a recent development, we will never sell your address. Prefer a weekly email?

    Nearly there — check your email.

    Industry observers note that we have sent a confirmation link to . Click it and you are on the list. If it has not turned up in a minute or two, it may be in your spam folder.

    Over the next two years, NPR will address a longstanding listener plea: improving its app.

    According to recent reports, during a November 12 board of directors meeting, NPR CEO Katherine Maher mentioned the organization will rebuild its digital offerings to be a “service-first, app-first destination” as part of NPR’s 2027-2029 strategic proposal, Current reported on Thursday. One goal of the plan is to reach “five million weekly active people on its platforms by 2029” and “to build a monthly engaged digital audience of 40 million.” According to Current, Maher said that the NPR network — which includes more than 200 member radio stations — currently reaches 39 million weekly listeners across broadcast and digital, but the “total potential addressable audience, weekly consumers of news, information and culture who are open to our work, is roughly 153 million Americans. That is nearly four times our current reach.”.

    Recent findings suggest that in Apple’s App Store, NPR’s app has a 4.7-star rating and more than 78,000 reviews, of which the majority are positive. But reviewers have quibbles.

    Industry observers note that bryan Moffett, NPR’s senior vice president of transformation, noted NPR+, the broadcaster’s subscription program, brought in $8 million in the 2026 fiscal year, up from $5.5 million in 2025. (NPR+ is available with a donation of $8 a month or more, and offers perks like podcasts without ads.) Maher said new investment in the app will help reach younger audiences and shift NPR’s “median audience age from 60-plus toward 40-plus.”.

    “We love radio, but we have been so wildly successful there that we’ve largely exhausted its further financial growth,” Maher told the board. “And as it shrinks, we must invert our revenue engine to ensure sustainability across all of our platforms, including radio, but to build a wider funnel through digital offerings, third-party platforms, and fresh investments in marketing and communication that will tell our story and share our value with the world.”.

    Recent findings suggest that RELATED ARTICLENPR, the quintessential audio news brand, adapts to a video-first futureSarah ScireSeptember 29, 2026Overhauling the app is just one part of NPR’s strategy to keep up with consumers’ changing consumption preferences. In September, Sarah Scire reported on the broadcaster leaning into video podcasts with the acquisition of Kevin Roose and Casey Newton’s technology podcast Machine Gods. NPR chief operating officer Ryan Merkley told Current in June that NPR was already working on redesigning the app to better serve member stations and their listeners.

    “Fix the app,” departing public editor Kelly McBride told NPR leaders during the meeting. “It’s not a great experience for the audience and it’s key to moving forward, but you guys seem like you’re on it. So I won’t dwell on that.”.

    Nieman Lab requested a copy of the approved strategic plan but did not receive it by publication time. Read the full story in Current here.
